Aligning a table caption to the left in LaTeX *without* the `caption` package is a bit more manual, as the `caption` package provides convenient commands for this. However, it's definitely achievable using standard LaTeX environments and font/paragraph manipulation.

Here are a few common methods, ranging from simple to more robust:

**Method 1: Using `\raggedright` (Simplest)**

This is the most straightforward if you just want to left-align the caption text itself.

```latex
\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[h!]
  \centering % This centers the table itself, not the caption.
  \caption{\raggedright This is my left-aligned table caption. It can be a bit longer and will wrap accordingly to the left margin.}
  \label{tab:my_table}
  \begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
    \hline
    Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\
    \hline
    Data 1   & Data 2   & Data 3   \\
    Data 4   & Data 5   & Data 6   \\
    \hline
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

**Explanation:**

*   `\raggedright` is a switch that changes the paragraph alignment for subsequent text to be left-aligned. It's similar to the `flushleft` environment but can be used inline within a `\caption`.
*   The `\centering` within the `table` environment centers the *table content*, not the caption.

**Limitations:**

*   This only affects the text *within* the `\caption{...}`. The "Table X:" prefix will still be at the default alignment (usually centered or left-aligned depending on your document class defaults).

**Method 2: Using a `minipage` (More Control, Centers the "Table X:" prefix)**

This method gives you more control over the width and ensures the "Table X:" prefix also appears left-aligned relative to the `minipage`.

```latex
\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[h!]
  \centering % Centers the *minipage* containing the caption + table.
  \begin{minipage}{\textwidth} % Make minipage the width of the text.
    \caption{\raggedright This is my left-aligned table caption. It's much longer and demonstrates wrapping within the minipage, and both the prefix and the text are left-aligned.}
    \label{tab:my_table_minipage}
    \centering % Centers the table *within* the minipage.
    \begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
      \hline
      Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\
      \hline
      Data 1   & Data 2   & Data 3   \\
      Data 4   & Data 5   & Data 6   \\
      \hline
    \end{tabular}
  \end{minipage}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

**Explanation:**

*   We wrap the `\caption` and the `tabular` environment inside a `\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}...\end{minipage}`. This creates a box with the width of the text area.
*   `\caption{\raggedright ...}`: `\raggedright` now applies to the entire caption including the "Table X:" prefix as it's the first thing in the `minipage`'s content flow that starts a paragraph.
*   The `\centering` before the `minipage` will center the entire `minipage` (which in this case is `\textwidth`, so it won't appear to move).
*   The `\centering` *inside* the `minipage` is crucial to center the `tabular` within that `minipage`. If you omit it, the `tabular` will also be left-aligned within the `minipage`.

**Advantages:**

*   Both the "Table X:" prefix and the caption text are left-aligned relative to the `minipage`.
*   You have precise control over the width of the caption (e.g., using a fixed width like `\linewidth` or a relative width).

**Method 3: Redefining `\fnum@table` and `\T@caption` (Advanced, Potentially Fragile)**

This method directly manipulates the internal LaTeX macros that control caption formatting. It's generally less recommended unless you truly cannot use the `caption` package and the other methods don't suit your needs. It can be sensitive to document class and other packages.

```latex
\documentclass{article}

% This code needs to be placed in your preamble (before \begin{document})
% --- Advanced: Modify internal LaTeX macros ---
\makeatletter
% Redefine the command that prints the "Table X:" part
\renewcommand*\fnum@table{\normalfont\bfseries Table~\thetable} % Default is \normalfont\bfseries Table\ \thetable:
                                                            % We remove the ":" for more flexibility with spacing.

% Redefine the caption format to always be \raggedright
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%  <-- Changed: added ": " between #1 and #2
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    \ifvoid\footins % For figures, ensure it's not a footnote-only page
      \raggedright #1: #2\par % Changed to \raggedright
    \else
      \raggedright #1: #2\par % Changed to \raggedright
    \fi
  \else
    \hbox to\hsize{\raggedright #1: #2\hfil}% <-- Changed to \raggedright and removed \centering
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
% --- End of advanced modifications ---

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[h!]
  \centering % Still centers the table, but caption is left-aligned.
  \caption{This is my left-aligned table caption using redefined internal macros. It will always be left-aligned globally for all tables without needing `\raggedright` inside each caption call, as long as it fits the line.}
  \label{tab:advanced_table}
  \begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
    \hline
    Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\
    \hline
    Data 1   & Data 2   & Data 3   \\
    Data 4   & Data 5   & Data 6   \\
    \hline
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[h!]
  \centering
  \caption{Another table to demonstrate that the change is global with this method. It's also left-aligned.}
  \label{tab:advanced_table_two}
  \begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
    \hline
    A & B \\
    \hline
    C & D \\
    \hline
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

**Explanation:**

*   `\makeatletter` and `\makeatother`: These are necessary to use `@` in macro names, which are internal to LaTeX.
*   `\renewcommand*\fnum@table{...}`: This redefines how the "Table X" part is formatted. I've removed the default colon and added one manually later (`#1: #2`) to have more control over the spacing.
*   `\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{...}`: This is the core macro that typesets captions.
    *   `#1` is the "Table X" part (`\fnum@table`).
    *   `#2` is the actual text you provide in `\caption{...}`.
    *   I've changed the lines that handle cases where the caption is longer than `\hsize` (paragraph mode) and shorter than `\hsize` (hbox mode). Both now use `\raggedright`.
    *   Note the insertion of `: ` between `#1` and `#2` to visually separate the table number and its description.

**Advantages:**

*   Globally applies left-alignment to all table captions without needing `\raggedright` in each `\caption`.

**Limitations:**

*   **Highly Recommended to Avoid for Beginners:** This is quite advanced and changes internal LaTeX behavior. It can clash with document classes or other packages that also modify caption formatting (including the `caption` package itself, which this method is specifically trying to bypass).
*   Fragile: Future LaTeX updates might change these internal macros, potentially breaking your document.
*   Less readable and harder to debug.

---

**Recommendation:**

*   For a one-off caption or if you just need the text to be left-aligned: **Method 1 (`\raggedright` inside `\caption`)**
*   For better control, ensuring the "Table X:" prefix is also left-aligned relative to the caption text: **Method 2 (using `minipage`)**
*   **Method 3 is generally not recommended** unless you have a very specific, global requirement and are willing to deal with potential compatibility issues. It's often better to just use the `caption` package.

If you find yourself frequently wanting to customize captions, seriously reconsider using the `caption` package. It's designed for exactly this purpose and handles almost all alignment, font, and spacing options gracefully.
